title: Win through Action, Never through Argument
summary: Winning an argument is fleeting because people naturally return to their deeply held beliefs. Winning through demonstration and action has a lasting psychological impact, as the mind easily grasps reality when it sees proof. Arguing wastes time and energy on those who lack your knowledge, whereas actions speak louder than words and leave no room for disagreement.
example: An engineer in old times argued with a general over the size of a battering ram and disobeyed orders by sending a smaller one, leading to his execution because he argued instead of demonstrating.
A skilled sculpture creator pretended to alter a statue's nose by tapping it and dropping dust while changing the mayor's viewing elevation, satisfying the mayor without an argument.
An architect named Wren designed pillars that did not touch the ceiling to ease a mayor's safety concerns without actually altering his cost-effective design.
Kissinger used a symbolic visit during tense negotiations to deliver a powerful, wordless message to Israel's committee about the consequences of negating the agreement.
reversal: Arguments are useful when playing a deception or trying to cover up a lie, as they can distract and confuse the opponent.
Lustig, a con artist, escaped an angry police officer by using overwhelming arguments, fancy terms, and fake notes to confuse the officer and keep his profit.
